quote: In addition, the other VEGF pathway inhibitors including small molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitors (sunitinib, sorafenib, and pazopanib), a soluble VEGF decoy receptor (aflibercept), and a humanized monoclonal antibody of VEGF receptor 2 (VEGFR2) (ramucirumab) have been approved for cancer therapy.
summary: Cancer review on resistance to anti-VEGF therapy that mentions VEGFR2 antibody ramucirumab; nothing on UC.

quote: Levels of VEGF-A and VEGFR-2 increased in samples from patients with IBD and colitic mice.
summary: VEGFR-2 was increased in IBD patient samples and in DSS colitis mice; VEGF-A overexpression worsened colitis while soluble VEGFR-1 improved it.

quote: In addition, stigmasterol markedly disrupted angiogenesis in human cholangiocarcinoma by tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR-2) signaling down-regulation.
summary: Review of stigmasterol pharmacology that mentions VEGFR-2 signalling down-regulation in cholangiocarcinoma; no UC data.
The review focuses on VEGF-C/VEGFR-3 lymphatic signalling in inflammation, not KDR/VEGFR2.

quote: Pre-clinical and clinical evidence suggests that simultaneous blockade of VEGF receptor-2 (VEGFR-2) and PD-1 or PD-L1 enhances antigen-specific T-cell migration, antitumour activity, and has favourable toxicity.
summary: Phase 1a/b trial of the VEGFR-2 antibody ramucirumab with pembrolizumab in cancers; treatment-related colitis occurred in 5% of patients but UC was not studied.
The paper studies VEGF-C/VEGF-D and VEGFR-3 lymphatics in skin inflammation, not KDR/VEGFR2.

quote: Although treatment with an anti-VEGFR-2 antibody inhibited skin inflammation, epidermal hyperplasia, inflammatory infiltration, and angiogenesis, systemic inhibition of VEGFR-3, surprisingly, increased inflammatory edema formation and inflammatory cell accumulation despite inhibition of lymphangiogenesis.
summary: In a mouse model of chronic skin inflammation, an anti-VEGFR-2 blocking antibody reduced inflammation and angiogenesis; the model is cutaneous, not colitis.

quote: The VEGF-C/VEGFR-3 and VEGF-A/VEGF-R2 signaling pathways are two of the best-studied pathways in IAL.
summary: Review of inflammation-associated lymphangiogenesis naming VEGF-A/VEGFR-2 as a key pathway; no specific new data on KDR.
Only VEGFR3 levels are reported in an ovarian cancer olaparib/durvalumab trial; KDR/VEGFR2 is not examined.

quote: The VEGF-KDR reactivity of the submucosal vasculature was only slightly increased in UC and CD compared with normal tissue.
summary: Immunohistochemistry showed VEGF-KDR activated submucosal vasculature was only slightly increased in UC and Crohn's disease versus normal tissue.

quote: We further demonstrated that this continuous regeneration process is mediated by Notch signaling and that the expression of the Notch ligand delta-like 4 (DLL4) in lacteals requires activation of VEGFR3 and VEGFR2.
summary: VEGFR2 is named as one of two receptors needed for DLL4 expression in intestinal lacteals; the study does not perturb VEGFR2 or test colitis.

quote: Furthermore, VEGFR-2 expression on activated T-cells and FoxP3high regulatory T-cells also allow a direct effect of VEGF-A.
summary: Review of VEGF-A effects on T cells in tumours noting VEGFR-2 expression on activated and regulatory T cells; no UC data.

quote: Dendritic cells (DCs), macrophages, and lymphocytes further express certain types of VEGF receptors.
summary: Review of VEGF/VEGFR signalling in immune and cancer cells with no UC-specific data on KDR.

quote: Recently, a first clinical grade ultrasound contrast agent (BR55), targeted at a molecule expressed in neoangiogenesis (vascular endothelial growth factor receptor type 2; VEGFR2) has been introduced and safety and feasibility of VEGFR2-targeted ultrasound imaging is being explored in first inhuman clinical trials in various cancer types.
summary: Review of ultrasound molecular imaging describing a VEGFR2-targeted contrast agent in cancer trials; IBD imaging is mentioned only generally.

quote: VEGF-A can regulate angiogenesis, vascular permeability, and inflammation by binding with VEGFR-1 and VEGFR-2.
summary: Review of the VEGF family in coronary heart disease that mentions VEGFR-2 binding; no UC data.

quote: Here, we have uncovered an immunosuppressive role for nonclassical Ly6Clo monocytes that mediates resistance to anti-VEGFR2 treatment.
summary: In mouse colorectal tumours, anti-VEGFR2 therapy led to Ly6Clo monocyte recruitment and resistance; no colitis outcome was assessed.

quote: Blockade of VEGF function via soluble decoy receptors suppressed tumor development, inhibited tumor angiogenesis, and blocked tumor cell proliferation.
summary: VEGFR2 was activated on epithelial cells in colitis-associated cancer patients, and blocking VEGF signalling suppressed tumour growth in a mouse colitis-associated cancer model.
